newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan paper says Eritrea rebels killed 83 soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan paper says Eritrea rebels killed 83 soldiers.

text.p: A privately-owned Khartoum newspaper said on Saturday Eritrean rebels had killed 83 of Asmara's soldiers and wounded more than 100 others in clashes on Eritrea's eastern coast.
The daily Akhbar al-Youm quoted unnamed Eritrean sources as saying the rebel Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) had launched the attack on a military camp in Ariri, near the Red Sea coast.

"The front's soldiers managed to destroy two tanks and some equipment belonging to (Eritrean President Isayas) Afeworki's regime... the attack resulted in the killing of 83 government soldiers and the wounding of more than 100," the daily said.
The newspaper did not say when the attack took place and the report could not be independently confirmed.
Ties between Sudan and Eritrea are strained over counter-claims that each country supports rebels fighting to overthrow the government.

Khartoum has also said that Eritrean soldiers are fighting alongside Sudanese rebels who launched an offensive in January to topple the Islamist government. Asmara denies any involvement in the fighting.

But Abdalla Idris, the head of the ELF and commander of the rebel coalition, was quoted in Akhbar al-Youm as saying that Eritrea had launched a "war of aggression" against Sudan with the help of Israeli arms and expertise.
He also said Asmara was the Jewish state's "best friend" in Africa. The Khartoum government has also said that Eritrea is working against it with prompting from Israel.
